extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators/Program Directors and other senior/key personnel preparing NIH-style grant biosketches and Research & Related budgets (grant applicants and institutional budget officers).
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing biographical sketches for senior/key personnel and completing Research & Related budget and budget justification sections of an NIH-style grant application, including required fields, page limits, and line-item justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH Provide the following information for the key personnel and other significant contributors in the order listed on Form Page 2. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified format for each listed person and respect the four-page maximum for an individual's biosketch. Include sections A–D in order (Personal Statement; Positions and Honors; Selected Peer-reviewed Publications; Research Support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Name, eRA Commons user name, and position title
rubrics_metrics.description: NAME, eRA COMMONS USER NAME, POSITION TITLE must be provided for each person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the exact name as used on forms, include the eRA Commons credential if applicable, and a current position title (e.g., Director, Preclinical Development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training entries
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, and include postdoctoral training.) INSTITUTION AND LOCATION, DEGREE (if applicable), YEAR(s), FIELD OF STUDY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List institution/location, degree, dates, and field of study in chronological order beginning with initial professional education and including postdoctoral training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A. Personal Statement — summarize relevant background and qualifications and describe relevance to the proposed project (example shows PI describing prior work, regulatory familiarity, leadership of similar projects, and proposed role in current application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section to explain why the individual is well suited for their role on the project, cite relevant experience, recent accomplishments, and specific contributions the person will make to the proposed work. Tailor content to the application aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positions and Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: B. Positions and Honors — list Positions and Employment, Other Experience and Professional Memberships, and Honors with dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide chronological employment history with dates and institutional affiliations, list professional memberships and notable honors/fellowships. Include dates for each entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selected Peer-reviewed Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: C. Selected Peer-reviewed Publications — provide a selection of relevant publications (example: 'Selected from 37 peer-reviewed publications').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select publications most relevant to the proposed project. Provide standard citations (authors, title, journal, volume:pages, year). The biosketch should not attempt to list all publications if lengthy — choose representative/most relevant works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Support (Ongoing and Completed)
rubrics_metrics.description: D. Research Support — list Ongoing Research Support and Completed Research Support entries including grant number, PI/role, project title, dates, role, and percent Effort/Time effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish ongoing vs completed support; include grant identifiers, project titles, dates, official role (PI, Program Director, Co-Investigator, Leading Investigator), and percent effort/time commitment for the budget period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow same biosketch format for all senior/key persons
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOSKETCHES for the Principal Investigator and all Co-Investigators — Follow this format for each listed Senior/Key Person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every senior/key person and significant contributor provides a biosketch conforming to the same format and page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Person budget fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Section A & B of Research & Related Budget require for Senior/Key Person: Project Role, Base Salary ($), Fringe Benefits ($), Funds Requested ($), Academic Months, Summer Months, Calendar Months, and Number of Personnel / Project Role entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all salary and effort fields for each senior/key person, showing requested salary, fringe, months of effort (academic/summer/calendar), and total funds requested specific to the budget period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Personnel budget details
rubrics_metrics.description: Section B – Other Personnel: Number of Personnel, Project Role, Academic Months, Summer Months, Requested Salary ($), Calendar Months; total other personnel and total salary/wages and fringe benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List all other personnel by role (postdocs, grad students, research associates, clerical if applicable), state percent effort (months), requested salary and fringe, and compute totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment listing threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Section C. Equipment — List items and dollar amount for each item exceeding $5,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an equipment line-item table for items > $5,000 with cost estimates. If no equipment is requested, state that no equipment budget is included and that required equipment is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel cost categories and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Section D. Travel — Domestic Travel Costs (Incl. Canada, Mexico and U.S. Possessions) and Foreign Travel Costs separated; include totals and justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize domestic vs foreign travel, provide number of trips, purpose, and basis for cost estimates (e.g., average non-refundable economy fare, nights at GSA lodging rate, GSA per diem rates). Include justification of necessity for project aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant/Trainee Support costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Section E. Participant/Trainee Support Costs — Tuition/Fees/Health Insurance, Stipends, Travel, Subsistence, Other, and Number of Participants/Trainees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If participants/trainees are supported, itemize each support category, state number of participants, and provide rationale for amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Direct Costs categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Section F. Other Direct Costs — Materials and Supplies, Publication Costs, Consultant Services, ADP/Computer Services, Subawards/Consortium/Contractual Costs, Equipment or Facility Rental/User Fees, Alterations and Renovations, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorize other direct costs and provide itemized estimates. In the example, major cost drivers are tissue culture reagents/growth factors, culture vessels, fluorochrome-labeled antibodies, and procurement of animals (mice) from specified vendors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and supplies detail and major cost drivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Section F.1 — Materials and Supplies: major cost factors include recombinant growth factors, media, culture vessels, fluorochrome labeled antibodies for flow cytometry, animals (e.g., up to 540 mice) from vendors or in-house breeding, and general laboratory supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain major categories and assumptions behind supply needs and cost estimates (quantities, vendors, types of reagents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultant costs statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section F.3 – Consultant: indicate whether consulting costs are requested. (Example: 'No consulting costs are requested').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If consultant services are budgeted, list consultant, level of effort, and fees; if none, explicitly state that no consultant costs are requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawards / Consortium budgets and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Section F.5 – Subawards/Consortium: provide budget for academic partner (direct costs plus indirect costs), include their budget justification and detailed budget as attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the subaward's direct and indirect cost amounts, attach their detailed budget and justification, and state role of subaward/consortium partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits percentage and coverage explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe benefits, which are X% of salary requested, cover payroll taxes, employee fringe benefits, and workers compensation insurance. (Example: 38.94%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the fringe rate used, what it covers, and apply it consistently to salary requests; base fringe calculations on institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs: rate, base, and cognizant agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Section H. Indirect Costs — Indirect Cost Rate (%) and Indirect Cost Base ($); include Cognizant Federal Agency contact info. Example notes: 'The G&A rate, currently at %, is used to support administrative, operational and contracting matters... rate is based upon a bilateral rate agreement date Nov 6, 2012 between Cellerant Therapeutics, Inc and HHS/ASPR/ACMG.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the applicable negotiated indirect cost rate and base, cite the cognizant agency and agreement date, and describe the types of institutional support covered by indirect costs (vivarium, IT, accounting, procurement, facilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification content and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget Justification should explain assumptions and how costs were derived, including laboratory resources to be used, personnel roles and percent effort, fringe benefits computation, equipment availability, travel assumptions, materials major cost factors, consultant/subaward arrangements, and indirect cost rate justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide narrative rationale for each budget section, specify how figures were calculated (e.g., number of trips, ticket class, nights), and justify why requested resources are necessary to accomplish project aims. Attach any bilateral rate agreement or supporting documents where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative budget totals and section summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide cumulative budget summaries across Sections A–F (Total Direct Costs) and include Indirect Costs (Section H) to compute Total Direct and Indirect Costs (Section I), and any Fee (Section J).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure totals reconcile across detailed line items and cumulative budget tables. Present clear totals for selected categories (personnel, equipment, other direct costs, indirect costs) for the budget period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational and administrative identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Include organizational identifiers and administrative fields such as ORGANIZATIONAL DUNS, OMB Number, Start and End Dates, Project Subaward/Consortium entries, and attachments for budget detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete administrative metadata fields required on Research & Related budget forms and attach supporting files (detailed budgets, justifications).
